name: veterinary_clinic_system_057_unlinked_lab_orphans
instruction: Run the lab result integrity audit for this episode under the batch code in ops_meta. A lab_results row is 'unlinked' if any of the following hold: (a) its patient_id does not resolve to a patients row; (b) the patient it references has status='transferred'; or (c) the patient exists and is active but has zero visit_records rows (a lab result with no originating visit is an orphaned order). For each unlinked lab_results row, update it in place: set orphan=true and orphan_note to the batch code. Do not modify any valid rows and do not delete anything. Also write one ops_reports row report='lab_orphan_audit' with batch_code, unlinked_count, missing_patient_count, transferred_patient_count, no_visit_count, and flag_breakdown (object mapping each flag to its count among the unlinked rows). If the audit row already exists for this batch, overwrite it. The rule precedence for categorisation is missing > transferred > no_visit (a row is only counted in the first matching category).
_max_steps_note: Measure via live gold run in QC session; do not guess.
_par_steps_note: Measure via live gold run in QC session; do not guess.

success_criteria.summary: From seed: 19 unlinked lab rows (missing_patient=0, transferred_patient=1, no_visit=18). Flag breakdown among unlinked rows: critical=1, abnormal=5, normal=13. All unlinked rows must have orphan=true and orphan_note=batch. All valid lab rows (23 rows, e.g., id=2,3,5,8) must remain byte-identical except for the ignored updated_at field. Exactly one ops_reports row report='lab_orphan_audit' for this batch with the counts and breakdown. Dual-path counts (Python vs SQL) must agree.

checks.expect: exactly 19 rows updated with orphan=true/orphan_note=batch; 23 valid rows unchanged
unlinked count and category counts recomputed via SQL and Python; both agree

hazards: lab_results id=7 (patient 27) is a transferred-patient orphan. patients id=27 has status='transferred' and species='feline'. A solution that only checks missing patient_id will miss it.

lab_results id=1 (patient 4, Serum chemistry panel, flag='critical') is an orphan because patient 4 has no visit_records. It is the only critical lab row, so a solution that ignores the 'no visit record' condition will both under-count unlinked rows and leave the critical orphan unflagged.

Valid rows such as lab_results id=2 (patient 8, Heartworm antigen, flag='normal') and id=3 (patient 13, CBC, flag='abnormal') reference patients that exist, are active, and have visit_records. Marking them orphan fails the canary check.
Rule precedence is missing > transferred > no_visit. Patient 27 has no visit_records but is transferred; the lab row must be counted in transferred_patient_count, not no_visit_count.
Re-running the task must not duplicate the ops_reports audit row or create duplicate orphan fields; the gold deletes then rewrites the audit row and updates already-orphan rows with the same values.

uniqueness_report.differentiation_note: Hardmode v2 expands the v1 'missing or transferred' rule into a three-condition reconciliation (missing, transferred, or no originating visit) and requires a grouped `ops_reports` audit row with a per-flag breakdown. The no-visit condition requires a join through `visit_records`, making it a multi-hop integrity task with dual-path verification.
